oneOf.description: Its bytes (standard base64) and its digest (`sha256:<hex>`).
Not given, and asking again won't change that.

ChatAgent.description:
The agent that wrote a message (M197): the machine whose grant it acted
through, and its name now. The message's author is the machine's owner.

session.description:
The session that posted, as its machine called it then (#429): an
agent block's title, or the Claude Code session's name. Display
only; never what a permission rests on.

ChatFile.description:
One attached file, as the reader sees it. `url` is control's, for the
room's readers only (a session cookie, or an agent's token): the same
path with `?download=1` downloads it.

mime.description: What the bytes were sniffed as, never what the upload said.

width.description: An image's size in pixels, when its header gave it.

ChatFileKind.description:
How a file is shown: `Image`, `Video` and `Audio` inline (only types
that are safe to render: never SVG or HTML), anything else as a card
that downloads.

ChatMessage.description: A message as the reader sees it.

agent.description:
Written by an agent on the author's machine (M197): shown as
"<name>'s agent on <machine_name>".

also.description: A reply that was also sent to the channel.

author.description:
The author's account, and their name now. Both are empty for a
deleted account.

deleted.description: When it was deleted: its text, quote and pane are gone.

files.description:
Files and images attached (#107), in the order they were chosen.
Empty for a deleted message: its files went with it.

imported.description:
Brought in from a machine's own threads (M124): the name it had
there. Someone with no account here (a tailnet login, an agent) is
shown under the machine's owner, by this name.

mentions.description: The accounts it mentions, and the agents (`machine:<id>`, M198).

parent.description:
A reply (#106): the number of its thread's first message. The
room's list has it only with `also`; the thread has it always.

quote.description: Lines the poster chose from a pane, copied in (decision 1).

reactions.description:
Who reacted with which emoji (#104), the first reaction first.
Empty for a deleted message and for archives brought in.

seq.description:
Its number in the room. Messages brought in from a machine (M124)
keep their old numbers, unless the room already had messages of its
own: then they're numbered 0 and below, before control's.

system.description:
Not something said but something that happened (#119): `author` set
the topic or pinned a message. Drawn dim and centered; never
counted unread, pushed, edited or reacted to.

thread.description: The thread of replies this message starts, once it has any.

via.description:
Posted for the author by a product (M237): a hud box's name, for a
review written there. Shown as "<name> via <via>". [`SYSTEM_VIA`]
with no author: a line the platform wrote (#122), shown apart, as
plain text.

ChatPane.description:
A pane a message names, as the reader sees it: whether its chip opens
for them (they may reach the machine), and the machine's name.

ChatPerson.description: Someone, as the reader sees them.

dnd.description:
They've paused their notifications (do not disturb, #115): a moon
on their avatar. Only that it's on, never until when or why.

ChatReaction.description: One emoji on a message, as the reader sees it.

count.description: All who reacted with it; `who` names the first [`MAX_REACTORS_SHOWN`].

mine.description:
The reader has: a person's own reaction, or for an agent reading,
its own (never the owner's, nor the agent's for the owner).

ChatReactor.description:
Someone who reacted: an account, and the machine's agent if it was
the agent reacting for them.

ChatSystem.description: What a system line tells of (#119).

kind.description:
`topic` (its `text` is the new topic, empty when cleared),
`description` (likewise), `pin` or `unpin`.

target.description: The pinned message's number, for `pin` and `unpin`.

ChatThread.description: The replies to a message, as one reader sees them (#106).

following.description: The reader follows the thread. Always false to an agent.

read.description:
The reader's mark in the thread (a room number), and the replies
after it that aren't theirs (only while they follow), and how many
of those mention them.

repliers.description: Who replied, the newest first, at most [`THREAD_REPLIERS`].

replies.description: Replies not deleted, and when the newest was written (ms).

Decision.description: Approve it once, or deny it.

DeployWork.description:
What a deploy's run applies (M219), for its machine to check: the
deploy's operation (`arugula deploy op v1`) and the approval an owner's
device signed over it, with the passkey assertion the hub checked.

approval_id.description:
The approval's id (`apv_`), for the driver to note where it records
it (chant's approve note).

roll_back.description:
For a roll back (M220): the earlier deploy it goes back to, and what
that ran. The plan names it too.

secrets.description:
The names of the secrets its driver gets: their values come only
from [`WORK_SECRETS`], while the run runs.

settings.description:
The environment's driver settings (M220): the plan names them, so
the machine checks them against the approved plan
(`arugula_e2e::drivers::planned`).

Doc.description: A Doc, without its sections: a list's row, and a view's head.

agent.description:
The agent session that made it as itself (aru-115): its `machine`
the session's id (`ses_…`), its name `Agent session <id>`.

author.description:
The account that made it, or "" once it's deleted, or for one an
agent session made.

sections.description: How many sections it has, and how many are written.

DocList.description: `GET` [`PROJECT_DOCS`]: a project's Docs, the latest changed first.

writer.description: Whether the reader may make one.

DocView.description: `GET` [`PROJECT_DOC`]: a Doc with its sections, in order.

writer.description: Whether the reader may write it.

DocWrite.description:
`PUT` [`PROJECT_DOC`]: what changes. `title` renames it. With `section`,
that section's body becomes `markdown` (and its heading `heading`, when
given); with no `section` but a `heading`, a section is added at the
end, written when `markdown` is given and pending otherwise.

FinishResult.description: What a turn's finish step did (M261), on the turn's report.

command.description: The command, as the spec has it.

output_tail.description:
The last of what it printed (stdout and stderr, at most 4 KiB):
only when it failed.

FinishStep.description:
A workspace's finish step (M261): a command (`just check`) the box runs
as the session's user, in its checkout, after each turn and before the
push. When it fails the agent gets one more turn to fix it, with its
output; when that fails too, the branch isn't pushed.

timeout_s.description: How long it may run, in seconds ([`FINISH_TIMEOUT_S`] when 0).

GrantRevoke.description:
The project's grants taken back, by any owner's device: every grant for
the project under `delegation` made at or before `at`. It names no
grant, so whoever relays it can't point it at another one; a grant made
after it is a new one.

delegation.description: The delegation whose grants it takes back.

agent.description:
The agent that opened it for its owner; or the agent session that
opened it as itself (aru-115), its `machine` the session's id
(`ses_…`) and its name `Agent session <id>`.

author.description:
The account that opened it (an agent's owner's), or "" once it's
deleted, or for one an agent session opened.

closed_by.description:
Who closed a closed one (an agent's owner's account), as its latest
`closed` event says: a list's row names them (UI audit #163).

closed_by_agent.description: The agent that closed it for its owner.

IssueEvent.description: An event on an issue's timeline.

actor.description:
The account that did it (an agent's owner's), or "" once it's
deleted.

IssueGithub.description: Where an issue was exported to on GitHub (M205).

more.description: There are more past the last one (`before` its number).

IssueQuery.description:
`GET /api/projects/{project}/issues`'s query. Each that's given narrows
the list.

before.description: Issues numbered below this: the next page.

labels.description: Labels, comma-separated: issues with every one.

limit.description: At most this many (default 50, at most 200).

q.description:
Search words, in the title or the body: each one (`dep*`: a word
starting with `dep`).

NewSection.description:
A new Doc's section: a heading, and its Markdown now or an intent for
later.

Operation.description: What a deploy applies, as approved.

planned.description: The hash of the deploy's `planned` event, hex.

source_ref.description: The commit's sha or the artifact's digest.

PasskeyAssertion.description: A passkey's assertion as the hub checked it (M218): each base64url.

ProjectGrant.description:
An owner's device saying the platform may start and instruct runs on
`project`'s hosted workspaces, under `delegation`.

owner.description: `team:<id>` or `account:<id>`, as the signing device saw it.

PushAsk.description:
[`WORK_SESSION_PUSH`]'s body: which session, and the ref it pushes,
which must be the session's own branch exactly.

clone.description:
A token to clone the session's repo instead, with `contents: read`
alone: a repo linked to the project that no box's setup cloned is
cloned at the session's start, shallow (Fleet 6). The same checks
as a push's. An older platform ignores it and mints a push's.

oneOf.description:
An installation token for the session's repo alone, with
`contents: write` and `workflows: write` (aru-115, amended), or
`contents: read` for a clone, minted for this push or clone: the box hands it to git in one process's environment, never
to a file, then revokes it at `revoke` (`DELETE`, the token as its
bearer). `expires_at` is GitHub's.
Not given, and asking again won't change that.

Report.description: One state change, signed by the machine that made it.

detail.description:
A JSON object's text, exactly as signed: an exit code (`exit`), a
pane (`pane`, `epoch`), or why it failed (`reason`).

seq.description: The event's number in the run.

sig.description: The machine's signature over `arugula run event v1`, hex.

oneOf.description: Kept: the run moved.

Kept before: the same event, signed the same (a retry whose answer
was lost).

Not kept, and sending it again won't change that. `now` is the run's
state when it moved on without this machine (canceled, say), and
`next` the event number it's at when this one's isn't it.

RollBack.description:
What a roll back goes back to: an earlier deploy of the same
environment that succeeded, and what its log kept of what it ran (for
chant→Fly: [`IMAGE`], and chant's release record, [`CHANT_COMPONENT`],
[`CHANT_ENV`] and [`CHANT_DIGEST`]).

Running.description: What happens to runs already going when a grant is revoked.

oneOf.description: They finish.
They're stopped too.

Secret.description:
One secret, by its name as an environment variable. Its value is never
printed (`Debug` leaves it out).

revoke.description:
A short-lived token's revoke URL (`DELETE`, the token as its bearer):
the box revokes it when its driver ends (M219).

oneOf.description:
The environment's secrets and the driver's short-lived tokens, by
name. Given once per run.
Not given, and asking again won't change that.

Section.description: One section: pending (`body` null) until it's written.

body.description: Its Markdown (the machine Doc's: `chart` and `svg` fences draw).

id.description: The Doc's own: `s1`, `s2`, … in the order they were added.

intent.description: One line on what it will hold, shown while it's pending.

rev.description: Counts the writes to its body.

SessionAction.description:
Something a person asked of a session that only its box can do: answer
its open question, approve or deny its open permission, or cancel the
turn under way (the session goes on). Stopping the session isn't one:
control moves it to `stopped`, and it leaves the work list.

by_name.description:
Its login (or the name the platform has for it), for the
transcript's "Answered by" note: empty from a platform that doesn't
send it.

id.description: `sac_` and 32 hex characters: the box does each once.

request.description:
The open request it answers ([`SessionDetail::request`]); `None`:
whichever is open.

SessionDetail.description:
A [`SessionReport`]'s detail: each kind fills its own fields (the
module's docs say which), and leaves the rest out.

actions.description:
The actions ([`SessionAction`]) this report carries out: `answer`,
`approve` and `deny` on the `needs_input` to `working` report;
`cancel` on the turn's `working` to `done`, or a heartbeat when no
turn was under way.

block.description:
The agent block the session runs in, on taking it, and on a parked
one's next turn, which runs in a block opened again (Arugula #215).

by.description: An `in_block` turn's: who typed its prompt, when the block says.

commits.description:
A turn's: `"SHA subject"` for each commit it made, newest first, as
the daemon's turn work has them (`arugula_proto::api::Work`).

diffstat.description:
A turn's: `git diff --stat` from its start to HEAD, shortened as the
daemon's turn work shortens it.

finish.description:
A turn's: what its finish step did (M261), when the workspace has
one. A failed one isn't pushed.

harness.description:
Taking a session (M264): the agent the box runs it on, which is
`claude` when the one asked for isn't on the box.

head.description: A turn's: HEAD after it, abbreviated.

in_block.description:
A turn's start that came from the session's agent block itself, not
from the thread's prompts: someone typed in the block (its Open
button), or the agent woke itself. It names no prompts.

model.description:
The model its agent runs on (Arugula #215), as the agent names it
(`Opus 5.5`), once the box knows it and whenever it changes; each
turn's report says it again. At most [`MODEL_MAX`] bytes.

options.description:
To `needs_input` for a permission: its option ids; for a question,
its first question's choices, by their labels (Arugula #214).

prompts.description: The queued prompts a turn starts with (`spr_…`).

pushed.description: A turn's: whether it pushed the branch (HEAD is on the remote).

reply.description:
A turn's: the agent's last message, at most [`REPLY_MAX`] bytes
(less when the rest of the detail needs the room). The platform
posts it in the session's thread: a review's as the review (M264),
any other's as the turn's answer. A box from before every turn sent
it sends it for reviews only.

typed.description:
An `in_block` turn's: the start of the prompt typed there, at most
[`TYPED_MAX`] characters; none when the agent woke itself. The
platform says it in the session's thread, as its own line (Arugula
#215), and it's never a prompt.

uncommitted.description: A turn's: how many paths it left uncommitted.

SessionIssuesAsk.description:
[`WORK_SESSION_ISSUES`]'s body: which session asks, and what. The
project is never named: it is the session's, and the platform finds it.

oneOf.description: A page of the project's issues, newest first.

One issue by its number in the project: it, its timeline and its
newest comments.

A comment on one, as the session's asker, labelled as posted by the
session.

A new issue, with the asker's rights, opened as the session's own;
its labels from those the project's issues already have.

A new Doc in the project, with the asker's rights, as the session's
own.
A write to one of the project's Docs that this session made.
One of the project's Docs, or with no `id` the list of them.

comments.description: Oldest first: the newest of its thread.

more_comments.description: There are older comments than these.

oneOf.description: Posted, as this message of the issue's thread.
Opened: the issue, and its page's link.
A Doc, as made, written or read, and its page's link.
The project's Docs.
Not done, and why (the agent reads it).

SessionIssuesOp.description:
What a session's agent does in its project: read, comment on and open
its native issues, and make, write and read its Docs (aru-118), nothing
else. The route kept its first name, `session/issues`, for the boxes
already calling it.

oneOf.description: A page of the project's issues, newest first.

One issue by its number in the project: it, its timeline and its
newest comments.

A comment on one, as the session's asker, labelled as posted by the
session.

A new issue, with the asker's rights, opened as the session's own;
its labels from those the project's issues already have.

A new Doc in the project, with the asker's rights, as the session's
own.
A write to one of the project's Docs that this session made.
One of the project's Docs, or with no `id` the list of them.

SessionPrompt.description: A prompt queued in a session's thread.

author_name.description:
The author's login (or the name the platform has for them), for the
transcript's "from" note: empty from a platform that doesn't send
it, and for GitHub's text, whose login is in `author`.

source.description:
`member` (a project member's, in the thread) or `github` (text from
GitHub: a PR's review, a check's log).

SessionReport.description:
What a machine says of one of its sessions, signed: its fields are
`arugula_e2e::session::Event`'s.

detail.description: A JSON object's text ([`SessionDetail`]), exactly as signed.

n.description: The machine's report number in the session, from 1.

sig.description: The machine's signature over `arugula session event v1`, hex.

SessionWork.description: An agent session on this machine's workspace that hasn't ended.

actions.description:
What people asked of the session that the box hasn't done yet,
oldest first: listed on every pull until a report names them done
([`SessionDetail::actions`]).

asker.description: The account it runs as: whose mention started it.

branch.description: The one ref it may push: `arugula/<8 hex of the id>-<slug>`.

finish.description:
The workspace's finish step (M261), if its spec has one: what the
box runs after each turn, before it pushes.

harness.description:
The agent it runs ([`HARNESSES`]): `claude` unless it says (M264,
a Try 3's sibling or a review). A box without the one asked for
runs `claude`, and its first report says which it ran
([`SessionDetail::harness`]).

model.description:
The model its agent uses (Arugula #215), one of [`MODELS`]: the
one its ask named ("use sonnet"), else its project's setting. `None`:
the strongest, which the box picks ([`DEFAULT_MODEL`] for Claude
Code, Codex's own choice for Codex). The box reports the one it runs
on ([`SessionDetail::model`]).

n.description: The machine's latest report's number: its next report is `n + 1`.

park.description:
Parked (Arugula #215): `done`, with no prompt listed, for at least
[`SESSION_PARK_MS`]. The box closes its agent block, keeping its
user, checkout and conversation; once it lists prompts again the
box opens a block on them, loading the conversation. The platform
lists a parked one's prompts only when the box has a running slot
for it ([`MAX_SESSIONS_PER_BOX`]).

prompts.description: Its queued prompts, oldest first: what the next turn starts with.

repo.description: The linked repo it works in (`owner/name`), if any.

review.description:
A review (M264, `@codex review`): read-only. The box runs no finish
step and pushes nothing, and its turn's report carries the agent's
reply ([`SessionDetail::reply`]), which the platform posts in the
thread.

state.description:
Its state as the machine sees it: `queued`, `working`,
`needs_input` or `done` (an `unresponsive` one is listed in the
state it was in).

workspace.description: The hosted workspace (`hw_…`) the machine is.

revokes.description:
Every revoke of the project's grants the platform holds, on every
pull, ready runs or not: a machine checks them against the grants
its runs going were started under, and stops those a `running stop`
covers.

sessions.description:
The sessions on this machine's workspace that haven't ended, for a
machine that takes them ([`TAKES_SESSION`]).

WorkItem.description: A run that's ready for this machine and hasn't started.

deploy.description:
A deploy's run (M219): the deploy it applies, with its owner's
approval, which the machine checks itself before it starts.

grant.description:
The project's standing grant the run starts under (M211), when it's
`pending` under one, and the project's revokes the platform holds.
The machine checks them against its own enrollment before anything
starts, and keeps the revokes.

last_seq.description: The run's latest event: the machine's first report is the next.

op.description: The S37 operation's bytes (`arugula op v1`), exactly as stored.

op_hash.description: Their SHA-256, hex: the machine checks the bytes against it.

workspace.description: The hosted workspace (`hw_…`) the machine is.
